name: The Five Voids of the Peacock Feather
previous_label: Urdhva Mukha Svanasana — Upward-Facing Dog (asana framing, retired 2026-10)

dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24, sequential, one verse per dhāraṇā for 1–16)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: śikhipakṣaiś citrarūpair maṇḍalaiḥ śūnyapañcakam | dhyāyato 'nuttare śūnye praveśo hṛdaye bhavet ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, checked against Singh, Wallis's concordance and Pradīpaka
sanskrit_variants: GRETIL e-text prints ma.ṅdalaiḥ (an encoding error for maṇḍalaiḥ).
dharana.rendering: For one who meditates on the five voids by way of the many-coloured circles in a peacock's feathers, there is entry into the heart, the unsurpassed void.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer; not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: the five voids are the five senses (their subtle sources, the tanmātras), seen like the circles of a peacock feather; one meditates in the heart. Singh also notes a double meaning: maṇḍala names both the circles in the feather and the five senses.
dharana.technique_name: The Five Voids of the Peacock Feather

checked_against: GRETIL, Pradīpaka and Wallis: verse text matches the technique
verification.notes: Door index = Singh dharana number, verified directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against at least one independent edition. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

numbering_variants.wallis_yukti: Y6 (Wallis groups verses 24–27 as one technique)

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 32 does not prescribe a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is the eye of a peacock feather: rings of colour around an empty centre, used as a picture of the five sense-fields converging on emptiness in the heart.
geometry.svg_hint: concentric coloured rings narrowing to a dark empty centre, set over the heart
geometry.honesty: Redefined in 2026-10: geometry now records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Converge
reaction.summary: School metaphor: the five scattered sense-fields gather like rings toward one empty centre. Label only; not a chemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: soft breath around the chest and heart area
breath.cue: Even, natural breath, about four in and four out. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Orient from the edges of the senses inward toward one centre
orientation.gaze: Eyes softly open on a feather or image at first, then closed
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The five sense-fields (sight, hearing, touch, taste, smell) as rings converging on an empty centre
attention.secondary: The heart as the place of entry named in the verse

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: For one who meditates on the five voids by way of the many-coloured circles in a peacock's feathers, there is entry into the heart, the unsurpassed void.
adiyogi.method_summary: Optionally look at a peacock feather or a picture of one, then close the eyes. Notice the whole sensory field (sight, sound, touch, taste, smell) as nested rings. Let detail dissolve toward the quiet centre at the heart, without chasing sensation or forcing trance.

honesty.disclosure: Door 009 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 9 (verse 32) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type stays school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's. The original honesty text is kept below in honesty.legacy, with retired posture names redacted; the verbatim text is at previous_file.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 009 is dharana 9, verse 32. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.
Reframed from the earlier posture framing on 2026-10-06; awaiting guardian re-review. The previous review covered the posture framing only.

legacy.disclosure: This [retired posture]↔VBT link is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device by door index, not ancient one-to-one canon. Some editions number the same verse differently (e.g. as yukti 6).
legacy.notes: School index D-009 maps to Jaideva Singh dharana 9 = verse 32 (five voids / peacock mandala → heart). Experiential affinity with open front-body and heart-band attention is noted but not claimed as ancient pairing.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain in wrists, low back, neck, or legs.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. If attention to the senses becomes overwhelming, open the eyes and look at one simple object in the room. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.

legacy_notes.open_seat_alternate: [retired posture] ([retired posture]) or [retired posture] with thighs down; or hands on blocks to reduce wrist extension
legacy_notes.contraindication_notes: General practice caution for loaded wrist extension and lumbar compression; not medical advice. If wrists or low back complain, regress to [retired posture] or skip.
legacy_notes.status: Posture-specific cautions, kept for traceability; they no longer apply because this door teaches no posture.

beats.title: Name the door
beats.script: This is Door 009: the five voids of the peacock feather. Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 9, verse 32.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: No shape to make. Any easy seat. The map is a peacock feather's eye: rings of colour around an empty centre.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Body supported. Look at a feather or picture if you have one, then close the eyes. Orient inward.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Even, natural breath, four in and four out. No forced hold.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Sight, sound, touch, taste, smell: feel them as five rings. Let them narrow toward one quiet centre at the heart.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: School image: scattered senses converge on an empty heart. Metaphor only.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: Verse 32: meditating on the five voids through the peacock feather's circles, one enters the heart, the unsurpassed void. Safe contemplative form only.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Open the eyes. Let the senses come back one by one: sound, light, touch.
